ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; (ii) Criminal Code s. 83 terrorism listing; (iii) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) OFAC SDN List and OFAC sectoral sanctions, due to USD payment rails via Stripe and PayPal; (v) FINTRAC administrative and criminal AML enforcement records; (vi) provincial securities regulators including the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) of Quebec. Identity verification must comply with FINTRAC's Customer Due Diligence requirements, including beneficial ownership verification at the 25% threshold. Although the esports platform is classified as Low_Risk_Standard and not a regulated money services business, full AML policy documentation and transaction monitoring protocols are still required by payment processors and Canadian banking due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises du Quebec online portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (for provincial QBCA incorporation); alternatively Corporations Canada online filing centre at https://isned-isde.canada.ca for a federal CBCA corporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the corporate name must be in French or include a French version that is compliant, with the French version given priority in all official records; an English version is permitted only where a valid French version has been approved, unless the name is a registered trademark under the Trademarks Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13). Names must use Latin characters with French diacritics; non-Latin scripts require transliteration. The corporate name must include a legal element (e.g., Inc., Corp., Ltée). The REQ will reject names that are not distinct, contrary to public order or likely to mislead, or that contain regulated tokens without prior authorization.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Insurance, Assurance, Fiducie (require licence or authorization from the Autorite des marches financiers)
Quebec, Canada, Federal, Municipal, Gouvernement, Royal (require express consent of the naming authority)
University, Universite, College, Institut (require permit from the Minister of Education)
Hospital, Hopital, Clinic, Clinique (require health authority authorization)
Lawyer, Avocat, Notary, Notaire, Chartered Accountant (regulated professions; require order approval)
Condominium, Cooperation, Cooperative (require specific statutory structure permits)
Police, Revenue, Agency, Commission (imply public authority; prohibited unless licensed)
Vapeur, Cercle, Club (regulated uses under the Civil Code and special acts)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations issued by the REQ are valid for 90 days and are not extendable; upon expiry, a new NUANS search and a new reservation application with a fresh fee must be filed. If the REQ refuses a proposed name: (1) file a written demande de revision (reconsideration request) with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching legal arguments, the NUANS report and, where helpful, trademark registrations or letters of consent from prior nameholders; (2) if reconsideration is denied, initiate judicial review before the Cour superieure du Quebec within 30 days of the denial (the Court may order the Registraire to accept the name if the refusal is legally erroneous); (3) alternatively, abandon the refused name and file a new reservation with a distinctive element; for a federal CBCA entity, a reconsideration request may be filed with the Director of Corporations under s. 313(5) of the CBCA within 30 days of the name decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for the registered office itself: the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises require a physical registered office address in Quebec where legal process may be served; post-office boxes and mail-only virtual offices are rejected by the Registraire. A serviced office with a real street address and service-of-process capacity, or a corporate services provider acting as registered agent, is acceptable. For a purely online esports community platform with no physical storefront, this structure is standard and does not, per se, trigger commercial substance deficiencies, provided the registered office can accept service and corporate records are maintained in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5% probability during the first fiscal year). Unannounced physical inspections by the Registraire, Revenu Quebec or the AMF are data-driven and rare for a low-risk online platform without payroll or inventory on site; probability rises materially if the company claims significant input tax credits without a demonstrated physical presence, commingles tournament prize funds, or engages in related-party transactions without proper transfer pricing documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 9-23, 36-106, 158 (articles of incorporation, registered office, directors, officers and by-laws)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, REQ), Immaterial Assets and Enterprise Registry Directorate
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed electronically with REQ, accompanied by the Enterprise Registration Statement (Déclaration d'immatriculation), resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation and assignment of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under the QBCA; shares may be issued at nominal value and consideration credited as stated capital. The board must have at least one director; if the board has two or more directors, at least 25% must be resident Canadians.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Corporation was duly incorporated under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, and the directors deem it expedient to organize the Corporation, IT IS RESOLVED THAT: 1. The incorporator's subscription for 1,000 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share is accepted and the shares are issued as fully paid against nominal consideration; 2. The registered office is fixed at [street address], Montreal, District of Montreal, Province of Quebec; 3. [Full Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Full Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer; 4. The directors are authorized to adopt by-laws, open banking accounts, and appoint external auditors; 5. All filing acts taken in the incorporation process are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate name query and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ - Online Name Search and Reservation Service (Recherche de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name search request on the REQ portal for a French/English corporate name; verify the name is distinct, lawful, and not prohibited; pay the CAD 31 name reservation fee and reserve the name for up to 90 days.
required_dossiers: Short description of the corporation's activities
Name Search Request Form (Demande de recherche de nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a second search or an alternative eligible name; objections may be cured under the QBCA name regulations within the original 90-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and electronic filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ - Online Deposit Service (Depot des statuts de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory articles form including corporate name, registered office municipality, share structure, business restrictions, first directors and incorporator; upload and e-file via the REQ platform; pay the CAD 365 electronic filing fee at the time of submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address any REQ notice of non-compliance by amending the articles and refiling; REQ will issue a clean certificate once all statutory conditions are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise registration, NEQ issuance and Revenu Quebec linkage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the articles, REQ files the Enterprise Registration Statement, collects the CAD 85.50 registration fee, issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ); key data is transmitted automatically to Revenu Quebec for opening provincial tax accounts.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request rectification of the register entry under QBCA s. 29; file a corrective declaration if registration data contains errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First organizational board resolution and statutory corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first directors' meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution; approve the pro-forma First Board Resolution, adopt by-laws, fix the registered office, appoint officers, open statutory registers, and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (minutes or written consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is procedurally defective, cure it through a new unanimous written resolution; no governmental remedy is required for internal corporate acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and provincial tax registrations and business accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Revenu Quebec - Mon dossier d'entreprise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST registration through CRA; concurrently open Revenu Quebec accounts for QST/TVQ, corporate income tax, source deductions if employees are hired, and supplier registers if applicable; execute intergovernmental exchange consents for streamlined registration.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution designating tax signatories
Payroll information forms if employees exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend tax account information by filing Revenu Quebec form ARQ-1038 or CRA Form RC59, as appropriate; late registrations are generally harmless if filed before the first taxable event.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ongoing annual compliance and minute book maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ (annual declaration) and the corporation's registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual declaration (declaration annuelle) with REQ before the anniversary of registration, update director and officer information, maintain the corporate minute book, document share transfers, and preserve financial statements in accordance with QBCA record-keeping requirements.
required_dossiers: Updated registered office and director lists
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a late annual declaration online and pay any late fee; if administrative dissolution occurs, apply for revival under QBCA s. 347 by filing all outstanding declarations and reinstatement forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the activity is a pure software/esports-host platform under ISIC 5820 and NAICS 711219; the Regie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) supervises gambling only, so no RACJ betting licence is required where the platform provides matchmaking and tournament management without betting on chance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required; if a live tournament venue is rented in Quebec, a municipal assembly permit (permis de rassemblement) would be the only event-based authorization from the local municipality.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Environmental Impact Assessment required; the corporation has no physical plant, no effluent discharge and no atmospheric emissions as a cloud-based software service
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital platform; if a future leased office or data-hosting facility is established, comply with municipal wastewater by-laws, CNESST occupational exposure limits for VOCs and MELCCFP noise standards for mechanical rooms

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable absent physical premises; any future office lease requires a municipal fire safety certificate under the Quebec Building Act, CNESST workplace compliance for ergonomic and electrical safety, and structural clearance for any event-specific public venue.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – My Business Account portal; for Quebec provincial tax, Revenu Québec – Clic SÉcur enterprise portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation must apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) through the CRA Business Registration Online service or Form RC148. If the corporation is federally or provincially incorporated, the CRA automatically issues a BN upon incorporation. Registration for GST/HST is effected through the same BN. Quebec QST registration must be obtained separately from Revenu Québec via Form LM-1 or the Clic SÉcur online service, using the same BN as a base identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election exists under the Canadian Income Tax Act or Quebec Taxation Act for a business corporation; all corporations are entity-level taxpayers. Elections available are limited to specific corporate reorganizations (e.g., section 85 rollover, section 88 wind-up), deemed year-end elections under section 249.1, and QST voluntary/immediate registration elections under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) – combination is administered federally by CRA and provincially by Revenu Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Canada (or Quebec for QST) in any single calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing API requirement currently applies. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices and XML/EDI records, but do not require pre-clearance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for zero-rating under section 23 of the Excise Tax Act when the goods are exported by the supplier by common carrier, or delivered to a common carrier for export, and proper export documentation is retained. Services supplied to a non-resident that are not performed in Canada are zero-rated under section 25; QST zero-rating rules under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax mirror these criteria for supplies exported from Quebec.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System record), including AES/CIES export report
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing shipment from Canada
Commercial invoice and proof of export contract
Bank confirmation or inward remittance certificate showing receipt of foreign currency payment
Cargo control or freight forwarder documentation where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the date of assessment, or indefinitely in the case of negligence, misrepresentation, or fraud. False export claims expose the taxpayer to gross-negligence penalties under section 163.2 (maximum 50% of the understated tax), interest, foreign-exchange gain reassessments, and, for serious tax evasion, criminal prosecution under sections 327 and 327.1 of the Excise Tax Act and section 239 of the Income Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF supervision; foreign exchange surveillance is indirect through market operations and the Currency Act; no designated foreign-exchange control administration analogous to a ministry of finance exchange-control division exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely convertible fiat currency without exchange-control licensing. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalized; Canada does not maintain a foreign exchange approval regime or repatriation permit framework for trade, dividends, interest, royalties, or capital injections. Profit remittance from a Quebec business corporation is unrestricted at the FX level, though outbound dividends and management fees are subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act; Quebec counterpart under the Tax Administration Act) and must be supported by auditable board resolutions and financial statements to satisfy the payer's withholding obligation. Sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, as well as FINTRAC cross-border reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000), remain the only practical gates on convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable: Canada imposes no surrender requirement, no statutory conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation timeline for export or service proceeds. Receipts in CAD or foreign currency may be held in any eligible Canadian or foreign bank account indefinitely. Reporting obligations are limited to (i) FINTRAC large cash transaction reports (CAD 10,000 or more), (ii) electronic funds transfer reports (EFTR) for international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more, and (iii) cross-border currency and monetary instruments reports for physical movements exceeding CAD 10,000, all under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada, Quebec-headquartered)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-conditioned viability. Offshore digital EMIs and payment facilitators (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) are permissible as ancillary settlement and payout conduits for foreign micro-disbursements, but a Quebec-registered esports platform must maintain its primary CAD treasury and tournament prize-clearing account at a CDIC-member Schedule I bank. Legal constraints: (i) under the Bank Act, non-bank EMIs cannot accept Canadian deposits for reinvestment purposes without a federal banking license; (ii) payment service providers operating in Canada must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act and establish a compliant risk-management and incident-response framework; (iii) USD settlements must traverse a US correspondent (Fedwire/CHIPS) to be compatible with Stripe/PayPal treasury cycles; and (iv) prize-pool fiduciary duties favor a segregated escrow designation linked to the tournament platform rather than an aggregated EMI float.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical board appearance exists under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, the Canada Business Corporations Act, or the FINTRAC AML/KYC framework. Remote account opening is legally permissible where the corporate applicant provides certified true copies of articles of incorporation, a certificate of status, the Quebec enterprise register (Registraire des entreprises du Quebec) excerpt, register of directors, and a beneficial-ownership attestation, plus remote identity verification for each signing officer and ultimate owner (credit-bureau-based, notarized, or video-verified). In practical Schedule I bank policy, the first operational account frequently requires an in-branch or video-conference signing ceremony for the corporate resolutions and signing-officer cards; fully remote opening is typically granted only when all directors are Canadian residents. Non-resident directors materially increase the likelihood of an in-person or video-recorded KYC interview mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding more than 25% of voting shares of the Quebec business corporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ultimate-ownership register filing (Registre des proprietaires ultimes), notarized passport copies and proof of personal address (less than 90 days old), an independent bank or credit-union reference letter, entity organizational chart with seat of incorporation, tax-residency certificate or equivalent treaty-based evidence, and a written source-of-wealth declaration for shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume tournament payout traffic structured as entry-fee-based prize pools, presenting potential money-laundering or unlawful-gambling characterization scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/ATF program compliant with PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; legal opinion or regulatory memorandum confirming skill-based esports competition classification outside the Criminal Code pari-mutuel betting prohibition and the Quebec Act respecting lotteries, publicity contests and amusement machines; tournament rulebook; KYC/KYB procedures for registered teams and organizers; prize-fund flow chart differentiating service fees from prize pool; and audited financial statements segregating sponsor revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency, stablecoins, or non-bank e-wallets for liquidity or player settlements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Digital-asset treasury policy restricting on-chain settlement; FINTRAC money-services-business registration evidence if the entity performs virtual-currency exchange or transfer functions; anti-fraud and sanctions screening procedures referencing the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (CCASL) and the Office of the Superintendent's guidance; user withdrawal and KYC audit-trail documentation; and a professional accountant's (CPA) verification letter confirming third-party origin of all injected digital assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparties and tournament participants located in sanctions-affected, high-risk, or FATF-monitored jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening log covering CCASL, OFAC and UN lists; documented adverse-media search; enhanced due diligence questionnaires for teams and corporate participants; a licensed-residence verification dossier (utility or bank statement) for payment beneficiaries; and a board-approved sanctions policy with escalation thresholds; remediation procedures for flagged counterparties must evidence timely disgorgement or denial.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound investor funding exceeding CAD 250,000 in a short period without clear underlying corporate purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder subscription agreement, board authorization resolution, bank reference for the remitting institution, explanations of fund provenance and shareholder wealth, MVP and go-to-market projection supporting capital deployment, and confirmation that no loans or advances are disguised equity without transfer-pricing backup under CRA section 247.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed via SWIFT with a precise remittance narrative, e.g., 'Share capital contribution - Esports Community Platform' or 'Intercompany loan - Esports Platform CA', including the legal entity name, Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), and the beneficiary bank's 3-digit institution number and 5-digit transit number. CAD wires settle through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the managed Real-Time Rail (RTR); USD wires clear through the bank's US correspondent (Fedwire or CHIPS). Canada does not impose a formal FX purpose-code schema, but FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting (EFTR) applies to international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more, and the receiving bank will require the remittance purpose to be captured for internal and CRA reporting. Intercompany capital surplus and shareholder loans must be contemporaneously documented with a written funding agreement, prescribed interest-rate benchmark, and transfer-pricing file in order to avoid Part XIII withholding characterization or CRA recharacterization upon later repayment. Verification of inbound routings is achieved via SWIFT gpi end-to-end tracking (UETR), the account statement, and a reconciliation against the corporation's cap table and share-purchase agreements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements employ (i) SWIFT MT103 for single high-value cross-border wires (e.g., sponsor fees, LC reimbursements, non-resident prize payouts above CAD 10,000); (ii) CAD domestic wire via LVTS or ACSS batch EFT for resident participants and operational vendors; (iii) commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for hardware, equipment, or licensed-content procurement requiring documentary compliance (proforma invoice, bill of lading, insurance certificate); and (iv) low-value mass tournament payouts via card-network payout rails or open-banking batch APIs integrated with the core payment gateway (Stripe/PayPal) to avoid MT103 fragmentation. A clearing-rail governance matrix must define acceptance rules, FX conversion point (account currency-level vs transaction-level), and settlement reconciliation timestamps. Prize-pool trust responsibilities require a segregated escrow account with dual-signature control where possible, and bank-provided sweeps into a CDIC-insured interest-bearing account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla CAD/USD deliverable spot and forward contracts (up to 24 months) transacted under an ISDA or bank master foreign-exchange agreement with a licensed Schedule I bank.
CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP forward contracts for tournament circuits in EU/UK regions, documented under a master FX agreement with mark-to-market and collateral posting.
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps (tenor 1-5 years) to hedge large prize-pool round-trip flows, requiring ISDA plus CSA and front-office update for non-financial end-user hedging.
Plain-vanilla FX options (CAD call/put) for pricing certainty on entry-fee conversions during peak tournament windows.

Canadian-dollar NDFs are contractually available from money-center banks but are economically unnecessary given CAD's full convertibility; their use is restricted and must be justified only where counterparty-balance constraints make an onshore deliverable forward infeasible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution; late compliance triggers notices and reinstatement costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after fiscal year-end; if fiscal year ends on December 31, due by June 15 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CAD $50 late fee; continued default leads to strike-off from the enterprise register, loss of corporate name protection, and possible administrative dissolution after notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for private corporations unless the corporation is a reporting issuer, shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand an audit (CBCA), or an external party requires an audited financial statement. Under QBCA, an auditor is required unless all shareholders waive the appointment by unanimous resolution annually.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations as applicable under CPA Canada

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the annual declaration must confirm the names and addresses of directors and indicate whether any shareholder holds at least 25% of the voting rights. Under the CBCA, if the corporation is federally incorporated, the annual return must confirm that the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) is accurate and up-to-date, including any transfers affecting significant control during the year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
